title: Card Skimming Device Deployment
description: A simulation demonstrating the mechanics of a card skimming attack. This involves installing a device to capture card data and a camera or overlay to capture PINs.
requirements: PIN Pad Overlay or Micro Camera
objective: To intercept and capture credit/debit card data (Track 2) and associated PINs from a public terminal (e.g., ATM, gas pump) using custom-made hardware.
principles: The attack leverages two key components: a 'skimmer' device that fits over the real card slot to read the magnetic stripe data as the card is inserted, and a hidden camera or a fake PIN pad overlay to record the user's PIN. The collected data can then be exfiltrated and used to create cloned cards for fraudulent transactions.

steps.title: Equipment Preparation
steps.action: Ensure the skimming device is fully charged and has sufficient storage. Prepare the PIN pad overlay or micro camera.
steps.detail: The hardware must be prepared to look identical to the target machine's components. Any discrepancy in color, texture, or fit can expose the device.

steps.title: Location Survey (Casing)
steps.action: Select a suitable terminal. The ideal location has high foot traffic but minimal direct surveillance or employee oversight.
steps.detail: Gas pumps and standalone ATMs are common targets. The goal is to maximize potential victims while minimizing the risk of discovery.

steps.title: Install Skimmer Device
steps.action: Discreetly and quickly place the miniature skimmer over the card entry slot.
steps.detail: The device should fit snugly and appear as a natural part of the machine. This is often done in seconds to avoid drawing attention.

steps.title: Install PIN Capture Device
steps.action: Position the PIN pad overlay on top of the existing keypad or place the micro camera in a position to view the keypad.
steps.detail: The PIN pad overlay records keystrokes directly. The camera must be carefully angled to have a clear view of the PIN entry.

steps.title: Data Collection Period
steps.action: Allow the devices to remain in place for a set period (e.g., several hours or a full day) to collect data from multiple transactions.
steps.detail: The longer the device is in place, the more data is collected, but the risk of discovery also increases.

steps.title: Retrieve Hardware and Data
steps.action: Return to the location to carefully and quickly remove the skimmer and PIN capture device.
steps.detail: This is another high-risk step. Once retrieved, the captured card data and PINs are downloaded for analysis and use.

tips: Use social engineering (e.g., creating a minor distraction) to divert attention during the installation and retrieval phases.
Bluetooth-enabled skimmers allow for remote data retrieval, eliminating the need to physically retrieve the hardware and reducing risk.
